review_notes: I read the whole file. It declares no simp lemmas, no @[simp] attributes and no definitions that need simp lemmas. It has three theorems: two iff criteria (pointwise convergence and continuity within a set) and one wrapper recovering Mathlib's normed-space result. I checked Mathlib's `continuousWithinAt_clm_apply` in Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Module/FiniteDimension.lean (and the ContinuousOn and ContinuousAt versions). Those are also not simp lemmas, and they are used via explicit simp_rw. The iff statements have a universally quantified right-hand side and are not canonical simplifications, so tagging them @[simp] would not be justified. Inside the proofs, `simp only [sum_apply]` and `simpa only [hs]` are local and cause no competing rules or cycles. I found no justified simp-interface problem. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about simplifier behaviour.
